issues.current: Hands-on staff need 24 hours of CE in the first year and 16 hours a year after, cited to 111-8-63-.09. Every new staff member needs first aid and CPR within 60 days.
issues.correct: Those details are ALC rules. For PCHs, rule 111-8-62-.09(5) requires 'at least sixteen (16) hours of training per year' for all direct care staff and has no 24-hour first-year rule. Under the ALC rule, first aid and CPR within 60 days apply to staff hired for hands-on services, not every employee. Under the PCH rule they apply to 'any person working in the home'.
issues.evidence: 111-8-62-.09(5): 'All direct care staff... must have at least sixteen (16) hours of training per year.' 111-8-63-.09(3)(a)-(b) lists first aid and CPR for 'staff hired to provide hands-on personal services'.
issues.fix: Split into PCH (16 h per year, first aid/CPR for all staff within 60 days) and ALC (24 h in year 1, then 16 h per year, first aid/CPR for hands-on staff within 60 days).

issues.current: On-site managers and supervisory staff must be 21+. Non-supervisory hands-on staff must be 18+. Cited only to 111-8-62-.09.
issues.correct: That is right for PCHs. For ALCs, 111-8-63-.09(1) requires the on-site manager and responsible staff to be 21+. Staff under 18 may work only with direct line-of-sight supervision, or at age 17 after a Georgia high-school nursing-assistant track.
issues.evidence: 111-8-63-.09(1): 'No staff person under the age of 18 is permitted to work... unless there is direct line-of-sight supervision...'
issues.fix: Add the ALC variant and cite both rules.
